text.text: These findings are also consistent with a recent systematic review of ego-dissolution and connectedness measures in classical psychedelic studies, which found that connectedness was associated with more durable mental health and well-being outcomes, whereas the effects of egodissolution were typically shorter-term (Kałużna et al., 2022).
text.formatted: These findings are also consistent with a recent systematic review of ego-dissolution and connectedness measures in classical psychedelic studies, which found that connectedness was associated with more durable mental health and well-being outcomes, whereas the effects of egodissolution were typically shorter-term <ref type="bibr" target="#b32">(Kałużna et al., 2022)</ref>.

text.text: Overall, our findings suggest that connection-and emotion-laden experiences appear more consistently aligned with positive persisting effects and lower acute negative affect.

Although causal inferences cannot be drawn from the present cross-sectional design, these associations are consistent with the possibility that fostering conditions that support connection, positive self-transcendent emotions, and a sense of interconnectedness may be particularly important for maximizing the lasting benefits of psychedelic experiences and for buffering against distress.

This interpretation aligns with theories of positive affect, such as broaden-and-build, which posit that positive emotions expand attentional and cognitive scope and facilitate the accumulation of enduring psychological and social resources (Huppert et al., 2004).
text.formatted: This interpretation aligns with theories of positive affect, such as broaden-and-build, which posit that positive emotions expand attentional and cognitive scope and facilitate the accumulation of enduring psychological and social resources <ref type="bibr" target="#b30">(Huppert et al., 2004)</ref>.

text.text: Psychedelic experiences may similarly engender broadened perspectives on self, others, and meaning, with downstream consequences for wellbeing.

Complementing this account, research on social connection and belonging highlights that feeling embedded in supportive relationships and larger social contexts promotes perceived safety and reduces threat sensitivity (Gilbert, 2024).
text.formatted: Complementing this account, research on social connection and belonging highlights that feeling embedded in supportive relationships and larger social contexts promotes perceived safety and reduces threat sensitivity <ref type="bibr" target="#b17">(Gilbert, 2024)</ref>.

text.text: Consistent with this framework, the observed associations between the Connection and Positive Emotions factor, spiritual-prosocial motivations, lower apprehensiveness, and fewer negative emotions suggest that this experiential profile may reflect a state of heightened social and existential safeness, in which feelings of connection and positive affect buffer acute distress and support enduring psychological benefits.
This study should be interpreted in light of its limitations.
First, it relied on retrospective self-reports of an experience up to five years prior.
Memory biases and post-hoc meaning-making may have influenced reports of the experience and its persisting effects.
Prospective, longitudinal designs that assess self-transcendent experiences and outcomes closer to real time would provide a stronger basis for causal inference.

Second, most participants endorsed recreational rather than therapeutic motives and given the small impact of substance type on outcomes observed in the current study (redacted-for-anonymizedreview), experiences involving cannabis, MDMA, and psilocybin were combined.
Although this diversity supports the generality of the identified components across substances and contexts, it limits direct generalization to clinical psychedelic-assisted therapies.
Future work should examine whether similar factor structures and associations emerge in formal treatment contexts.

Furthermore, although the factor solution showed good fit and internal adequacy, it was derived from a single sample; replication and confirmatory factor analyses are needed to establish its robustness and generalizability.

Finally, the modest variance explained in negative emotions and positive persisting effects models reminds us that self-transcendent experiences are only one set of influences among many-including other subjective experiences (e.g., emotional breakthrough, psychological insight; Kangaslampi, 2023), integration processes, social context, broader life circumstances-that shape long-term outcomes.
Several measure-related considerations bear noting.

Some constructs (e.g., small self, self-other overlap) were represented by single or few items; more comprehensive measurement of these domains may reveal additional nuance in their relations to other selftranscendent components.
Moreover, the present study included a relatively small subset of measures.

While this approach reduced item redundancy and response fatigue, future work could include other related measures, such as the ego dissolution inventory (Nour et al., 2016), Watt's connectedness scale (Watts et al., 2022) or the Awe Experience Scale (Yaden et al., 2018) to evaluate the robustness and generalizability of the observed factor structure.
text.formatted: While this approach reduced item redundancy and response fatigue, future work could include other related measures, such as the ego dissolution inventory <ref type="bibr" target="#b42">(Nour et al., 2016</ref>), Watt's connectedness scale <ref type="bibr" target="#b60">(Watts et al., 2022)</ref> or the Awe Experience Scale <ref type="bibr" target="#b70">(Yaden et al., 2018)</ref> to evaluate the robustness and generalizability of the observed factor structure.

text.text: Relatedly, future studies would benefit from assessing a broader range of conceptually related constructs (e.g., spiritual experiences, somatic experiences, perceived meaningfulness) to determine whether additional dimensions may form part of the phenomenological blueprint of self-transcendent experience.

Somatic experiences (e.g., chills, goosebumps, shaking, physical connectedness), in particular, have been identified as a core phenomenological feature of self-transcendent emotions and psychedelic experiences in prior qualitative and theoretical work (Garcia-Romeu et al., 2015; Yaden et al., 2018), yet were not assessed in this study.
text.formatted: Somatic experiences (e.g., chills, goosebumps, shaking, physical connectedness), in particular, have been identified as a core phenomenological feature of self-transcendent emotions and psychedelic experiences in prior qualitative and theoretical work <ref type="bibr" target="#b16">(Garcia-Romeu et al., 2015;</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b70">Yaden et al., 2018</ref>), yet were not assessed in this study.

text.text: Finally, incorporating a wider array of measures-including measures not commonly administered within psychedelic research (as we did with the Small Self, Inclusion of Self in Other and modified Differential Emotion scales)-may further bridge psychedelic science with broader contemplative, affective, and transcendental literatures.

Future research could build on the present findings by testing whether connection/positive emotion-related versus dissolution-related experiences differentially mediate symptom or wellbeing outcomes, by experimentally manipulating aspects of set and setting hypothesized to preferentially foster specific types of subjective experiences, and by examining how challenging self-transcendent experiences interact with integration and support processes to yield growth versus harm.

Although our data are purely phenomenological and do not test underlying mechanisms, they point to the value of future work examining whether distinct neurological mechanisms may underlie experiences characterized by Connection and Positive Emotions versus Time, Space, and Self-Transcendence.

How psychedelic-induced subjective experiences are linked to neurobiological or perceptual factors, such as "brain entropy" (Rankaduwa & Owen, 2023), deictic or perspective-taking processes (Hayes et al., 2001), or changes in functional connectivity within association networks, such as the default-mode network (Kwan et al., 2022), remains an open area of inquiry (Yu et al., 2024).
text.formatted: How psychedelic-induced subjective experiences are linked to neurobiological or perceptual factors, such as "brain entropy" <ref type="bibr" target="#b46">(Rankaduwa & Owen, 2023)</ref>, deictic or perspective-taking processes <ref type="bibr" target="#b28">(Hayes et al., 2001)</ref>, or changes in functional connectivity within association networks, such as the default-mode network <ref type="bibr" target="#b35">(Kwan et al., 2022)</ref>, remains an open area of inquiry <ref type="bibr" target="#b71">(Yu et al., 2024)</ref>.

text.text: In summary, this study provides initial evidence that psychedelic-occasioned selftranscendent experiences can be meaningfully organized into at least two correlated higherorder components-one centered on connection and positive emotions, and another on loss of one's sense of time, space boundaries, and self.

These components show distinct relationships with mindset, acute affect, and persisting positive effects, supporting a multidimensional conceptualization of self-transcendent and mystical experiences.
